thread:
ethan: Heads-up: Go sampleapp has a weird redaction+otel interaction when REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=warn. Request-id header gets scrubbed from logs but remains in spans. New users see blank request-id in logs which makes trace linking hard.

priya: can you share repro steps? which middleware is responsible for request-id in the Go example?

ethan: repro (local):
```bash
git clone github.com/redwood/sampleapp
cd examples/go
go run ./cmd/server
# env: REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=warn
curl -v http://localhost:8080/chat
```
Observed: server log prints "request-id: [REDACTED]" while OTEL span attribute shows the real id (e.g., "rid-go-123"). If log level is info or debug the header is visible. Seems tied to the redaction sanitizer only running at warning+ levels.

carla: interesting. our redaction pipeline is enabled by default but has conditional behavior for higher log levels to avoid leaking secrets in noisy logs. It shouldn't redact request-id though. Any chance the sanitizer pattern matches the generate ID format?

ethan: looked into sanitizer rules: there's a regex that redacts anything matching ^rid-.* as a potential PII marker for older mobile IDs. We recently tightened that rule and gate it to warn level. That explains why info shows the raw value. But it still feels wrong to redact request-id since we use it as a correlation key.

priya: +1. Request IDs are not PII and should be exempt. Two actionable items: 1) exempt request-id/x-request-id from redaction regardless of log level; 2) add an OTEL->logs reconciliation check in sampleapp tests so we fail if span and log ids diverge.

ethan: workaround I used: set REDWOOD_LOG_REDACT_EXCEPTIONS=request-id,x-request-id in env before starting. But onboarding users won't know to do that.

carla: thanks for the workaround. I'll update the sanitizer config to whitelist header keys and add a unit test in the Go example. Also we should update docs/quickstarts to call out the env var to avoid confusion.

priya: also add a small lint in our telemetry CI: run sampleapps at warn level and ensure logs contain an unredacted request-id and that it matches OTEL span attribute. That will catch regressions.

onboarding-bot: created issue #4780: "whitelist request-id from redaction; add reconciliation test for Go sampleapp" assigned to @carla. staging redeploy scheduled.

ethan: thanks folks. this should cut down on support tickets where customers say "I can see trace in console but logs show [REDACTED]." :thumbsup:
